dedupe_keys.name: space weather effects on critical infrastructure briefing on solar activity gnss and telecom impacts and hungarian forecast centres arxiv 2306 16380

description: This short briefing introduces solar activity phenomena and describes in detail how space weather affects critical infrastructure: gas pipelines, transmission lines, overhead wires, transformers, GNSS navigation and telecommunication systems. It explains that satellites carrying telecommunication, navigation and meteorological payloads sit in a radiation environment shaped by the Sun, that the ionosphere's conductivity and transparency depend on solar radiation, and that magnetic variations induce currents in long conductors. The authors then describe the Hungarian national and global space weather forecast centres and capabilities, and give guidelines for preparing for extreme space weather events. Producer: Gábor Facskó, Gergely Koban, Nikolett Biró and Munkhjargal Lkhagvadorj. Coverage: global, with a Hungarian focus on forecasting. Access: free arXiv PDF; the abstract was read and the rest was skimmed only. Licence and cost: free; licence CC-BY-4.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page) on the PDF. Caveats: it is an educational briefing, not a dataset or model, and numbers on impacts were not checked. Simulation uses: it gives reference context for hazard-exposure and resilience scenarios that include GNSS and telecom outages caused by space weather. Related records: the JRC space weather and critical infrastructures report (data-jrc-space-weather-critical-infrastructures-findings-outlook-2016) and NOAA SWPC products (data-noaa-swpc-products).
